excerpts.text: **Mount Elbert** is the [highest summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mountain_peaks_of_the_Rocky_Mountains#Highest_prominent_summits "List of mountain peaks of the Rocky Mountains") of the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") of North America. With an [elevation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevation "Elevation") of 14,440 ft (4,400 m), it is also the highest point in the [U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") and the second-highest summit in the [contiguous United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States") after [Mount Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Whitney "Mount Whitney"), which is slightly taller. The [ultra-prominent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra-prominent_peak "Ultra-prominent peak") [fourteener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteener "Fourteener") is the highest peak in the [Sawatch Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawatch_Range "Sawatch Range"), as well as the highest point in the entire [Mississippi River drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River#Watershed "Mississippi River"). Mount Elbert is located in [San Isabel National Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Isabel_National_Forest "San Isabel National Forest"), 12.1 mi (19.4 km) southwest ([bearing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_bearing "Absolute bearing") 223°) of the city of [Leadville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadville,_Colorado "Leadville, Colorado") in [Lake County, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_County,_Colorado "Lake County, Colorado").[[4]](#cite_note-NGS-4)[[3]](#cite_note-PB-3)[[5]](#cite_note-GNIS-5)[[a]](#cite_note-7)

excerpts.text: Originally measured as 14,433 feet (4,399 m) in height, Mount Elbert's elevation was later adjusted to 14,440 feet (4,400 m) following a re-evaluation of mapped elevations, which sparked protests. The actual change was made in 1988 as a result of the [North American Vertical Datum of 1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Vertical_Datum_of_1988 "North American Vertical Datum of 1988"); it seems the original measurement resulted from the Sea Level Datum of 1929.[[8]](#cite_note-Elbert-9)[[17]](#cite_note-18)[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEnright200912-17) A matter of some contention arose after the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") over the heights of Elbert and its neighbor [Mount Massive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Massive "Mount Massive"), which differ in elevation by only 12 feet (3.7 m).
